roadmap.goal: A committed OpenAPI 3.1 description served without a token at /api/v1/openapi.json, held to the code by a three-layer drift check, kept on the release by cargo xtask openapi, and tryable at a self-hosted /docs/api page.
roadmap.scenario_ownership_invariant: 53 scenarios (163 rows) and 54 stubs (41 xtask, 8 conformance, 5 docs page), each owned by exactly one step. Deviations from DISTILL: 01-04 retired as validation-only (its stubs are re-mapped and the id is unused); scenarios 22, 23 and 25 moved to 02-02 (token rows). @pending left after each step: 43, 41, 37, 33, 26, 17, 16, 8, 0. Ignored stubs: 49, 37, 22, 17, 15, 14, 13, 9, 0.

pending_id_remap.rule: Change a moved stub's ignore reason and panic id before un-ignoring it.

roadmap.release_gates: DEVOPS R1-R7. R2 at 01-05. R4: slices 01 and 02 ship in one tag, never from a tree holding PENDING_OPERATIONS (01-02 to 02-02). R3 at 03-03. R7: each step's CHANGELOG line is named in its notes. No push or tag without the user's go.
roadmap.standing_rules: TEST PARADIGM: example-based (project CLAUDE.md). DISTILL owns the scenarios, the driver and each stub's intent: un-pend or un-ignore only in the owning step, never re-author, and send driver failures back to the test owner. LANES: run lane_env first and lane_common last. Keep Docker up. Run aod_warm before acceptance, because the suite uses a prebuilt foundry and the drift driver runs target/debug/xtask. Every aod-0N count must be non-zero. Rerun the us-04 flake alone. Count xtask stubs with pending_gold!( because their step id sits on its own line. MUTATION: >= 80% on modified Rust; non-Rust faults per DEVOPS Mutation testing strategy 3. COMMIT: one local commit per step; no push, tag or PR. aod_pre is diagnostic (always exits 0): read its output, and stop if it shows a stale acceptance process or a foreign listener on the test ports. aod_mut runs before the step's commit, after `git add -N` so new files are in the diff.
roadmap.lane_env: set -o pipefail; export CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_BUILD_OVERRIDE_STRIP=false RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 EV=target/aod-evidence; mkdir -p $EV; aod_pre() { timeout 30 lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN | grep -i acceptanc; timeout 30 pgrep -fl 'cargo|foundry-acceptance'; true; }; aod_warm() { timeout 2400 cargo build --release -p foundry-app --bin foundry && timeout 1200 cargo build -q -p xtask && for i in 1 2 3; do timeout 300 target/release/foundry --version || true; done; }; aod_lane() { FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=$1 timeout 5400 cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --release --test acceptance 2>&1 | tee $EV/$1.log; }; aod_mut() { a=(); for f; do a+=(--file "$f"); done; timeout 60 git add -N . && timeout 60 git diff HEAD > $EV/step.diff; timeout 14400 cargo mutants -j 1 --in-diff $EV/step.diff "${a[@]}"; }
roadmap.evidence_dir: target/aod-evidence/ ($EV, gitignored): downloads, lane logs, diffs, ci.log
lane_common: aod_warm && env -u FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS timeout 5400 cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --release --test acceptance

Other methods on the description's address, or addresses beside it, answer the API's uniform not-found
The description is valid OpenAPI 3.1, names no instance, and its list-issues answers match what the server sends
scenario_name: An integrator downloads the API description from the instance without a token
The description an instance serves is the one committed in the repository
A bad or stale credential does not change the answer
The description names nothing about the instance serving it
Two instances running the same release serve the same description
An address next to the description still answers the API's not-found
Anything but reading the description's address answers the API's not-found
Reading the description needs no credential, and every API operation asks for the machine token
Listing a project's issues answers the way the description says
A refused list of a project's issues answers the way the description says
new, DIST-5 names: document_is_valid_openapi_3_1, wire_shapes_match_document, info_version_is_the_release, document_carries_the_d14_copy, document_names_no_instance

aod_warm && for t in aod-01 us-w05a us-w05c token-management-api pl-02; do aod_lane $t || break; done

Document per DDD-2/5-8 and DIST-7; serving per DDD-3/4 and Changed Assumption 1; unit tests per Test Seams and DDD-11/12/12a. The 401 stub excludes the credential-less description route. Until 02-02 the shape test covers only the components present. CHANGELOG: Added (01+02), Unchanged. STANDING.

steps.name: Operations drift rule with the pending-operations list
steps.description: check-arch rule api-openapi-operations: the code's routes, parameters, bodies and success answers equal the described operations, failing closed. Not-yet-described operations sit on one pending list. Un-ignores 12 stubs; un-pends 14, 15.
criteria: A route and operation mismatch in either direction fails the check, naming method and path
A wrong parameter, request body or success answer fails the check, naming the difference
Any undescribed operation fails the check, naming it, except operations not yet in scope for this slice
scenario_name: An operation missing from the description fails the build
A described operation the code no longer offers fails the build

steps.implementation_notes: Rule 1 per DESIGN check-arch Rules 1 (i-vii), ADR-API-OPENAPI-001 and OQ-D4 (share the no-mint parser). Per DDD-14 the pending list holds the 7 operations D13 names. Keep the pending set a rule input so that operations_tolerates_only_pending_operations survives its deletion in 02-02; retiring that test is the acceptance designer's call. STANDING.

steps.name: Statuses drift rule with its soundness clause
steps.description: check-arch rule api-openapi-statuses: each operation's statuses, body kinds and error codes, derived from the code by reachability, equal the description's. Un-ignores 15 stubs; un-pends 11, 12, 13, 17.
criteria: An answer the code can give but the description omits, or the reverse, fails the check
Anything the rule cannot read fails the check instead of contributing nothing
A passing drift check states which two description rules it applied and what it compared
The pre-release checks include the drift check
scenario_name: The drift check passes on the current tree, and says what it compared
A field the description lacks fails the build
An answer the description does not list fails the build
A wording-only change to the description passes
lane_commands: timeout 900 cargo test -p xtask && timeout 30 grep -c 'pending_gold!(' xtask/src/check_arch.rs

steps.name: Description refresh command, image-build check, release steps
steps.description: cargo xtask openapi [--check] [--root <dir>], with --root defaulting to the workspace root: the refresh sets only the version, and --check is read-only. The image build runs --check. RELEASING.md gains the steps. Un-ignores 5 stubs; un-pends 16, 18-20.
criteria: After a bump, one command updates only the description's version, and a rerun changes nothing
The read-only check refuses a stale description, naming both versions and the fix, and changes nothing
No image builds from a stale description
scenario_name: A committed description left behind by a release bump fails the build
One command brings the committed description up to a new release, and changes nothing else
Refreshing a description that is already current changes nothing
Checking a description left behind by a release bump refuses it, and changes nothing

steps.implementation_notes: Contract per DESIGN Contract Shapes, DDD-13 and DIST-4. Dockerfile per DEVOPS Release flow option A. The L2 test (DESIGN Handoff) fails naming the Dockerfile when the check is missing or misordered. RELEASING.md gets the DEVOPS Release flow edits (P4). CHANGELOG: Releasing. STANDING.

A refused issue or comment call answers the way the description says
